study_identification.title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

study_characteristics.study_objective: To quantitatively estimate the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD by integrating normative modeling and non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to identify latent disease factors, associate them with clinical characteristics, reconcile group-level and subject-level findings, and uncover putative OCD subtypes.

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12 (Computational Anatomy Toolbox); VBM preprocessing including segmentation into gray matter, white matter, and CSF; normalization to MNI space; resampling to 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.5 mm; nonlinear modulation; smoothing with 6-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel; TIV computed; Image Quality Rating (IQR) recorded
preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The preprocessing pipeline is described in detail, including software (CAT12), key steps, and parameters.
preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: We obtained GMV for each subject using the Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT12, http://dbm.neuro.uni-jena.de/cat12/). Main steps included: (i) segmenting images into gray matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid; (ii) normalizing segmented images into Montreal Neurological Institute space and resampled them to 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.5 mm; (iii) nonlinear modulation; and (iv) the gray matter images were smoothed with an 6-mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel (Ashburner 2009; Han et al. 2021). We also calculated the total intracranial volume (TIV) for the following analysis. The Image Quality Rating (IQR) combing image noise contrast ratio, inhomogeneity contrast ratio and root mean square was recorded to assess images quality (Brown et al. 2019; Han, Xu, Guo, Fang, Wei, et al. 2022a, 2022b, 2022e).

deviation_metric.answer: Voxel-wise Z-scores; positive Z-scores indicate increased GMV compared to normative prediction; negative Z-scores indicate decreased GMV; Z-scores were divided into positive and negative parts and handled separately for NMF; factor compositions (weights) represent individual's expression of each disease factor
deviation_metric.reason: The study clearly describes the deviation metric as voxel-wise Z-scores, calculated by quantifying the deviation between predicted and observed GMV, normalized by prediction uncertainty. The Z-scores were then separated into positive and negative components for input to NMF.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: For each voxel, the Z-score was obtained by quantifying the deviation between the predicted GMV and the true one then normalized by the uncertainty of prediction. The positive Z-scores suggested increased GMVs than expected in patients than HCs and vice versa. We divided voxel-wise morphological differences into increased and decreased parts according to Z-scores. For decreased parts, the Z-scores were multiplied by -1. The following step was performed in increased and decreased parts separately.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Pearson correlation coefficients calculated between factor compositions (weights) and clinical characteristics including illness duration, age of onset, and Y-BOCS total score. Two-sample t-tests performed to examine sex differences in factor compositions. Linear regression model constructed to predict group-level differences (unthresholded T-map from two-sample t-test controlling for age, sex, and TIV) from the identified disease factors; coefficients of this model treated as factor composition of the 'average patient'. Affinity propagation clustering applied to factor compositions to identify putative OCD subtypes. Two-sample t-tests conducted to compare GMV between each subtype and HCs (SPM12, FDR corrected P<0.05, cluster size >100 voxels). All correlation analyses were FDR corrected.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Four robust disease factors (2 positive, 2 negative) were identified; each patient expressed multiple factors with unique compositions that correlated with symptom severity, age of onset, illness duration, and sex; group-level case-control differences were quantitatively derived from these factors; two subtypes with opposite GMV patterns were identified.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Four robust disease factors were identified via NMF (2 positive, 2 negative) with distributions involving vmPFC, striatum, insula, thalamus, putamen, hippocampus, and temporal regions. Patients showed notable interindividual variations in factor compositions. Positive factor 2 (PW2) negatively correlated with illness duration (r=-0.283, FDR-corrected P=0.035) and age of onset (r=-0.336, FDR-corrected P=0.020). Negative factor 1 (NW1) and negative factor 2 (NW2) positively correlated with Y-BOCS total score (r=0.242, P=0.049 for NW1; r=0.266, P=0.035 for NW2). Female patients showed significantly lower PW2 (t=-2.303, Cohen's d=-0.466, FDR-corrected P=0.047) and higher NW2 (t=2.319, Cohen's d=0.469, FDR-corrected P=0.047) than males. Robust analysis (80% patient subsets, 100 iterations) confirmed factor stability. LOOCV demonstrated strong prediction of factor compositions for unseen patients (R²=0.862 for PW1, R²=0.903 for PW2, R²=0.735 for NW1, R²=0.806 for NW2; all permutation P<0.001). Group-level unthresholded T-map was significantly predicted from disease factors (R²=0.700, P<0.001). Affinity propagation clustering identified 2 subtypes (n=35, n=63) with no clinical differences but significant differences in factor compositions: subtype 1 had higher positive factor weights (PW1: t=6.153, d=1.297; PW2: t=5.597, d=1.180) and lower negative factor weights (NW1: t=-3.716, d=-0.783; NW2: t=-7.494, d=-1.580; all FDR P<0.001). Subtype 1 showed significantly increased GMVs while subtype 2 showed decreased GMVs compared to HCs in distributed brain regions (FDR P<0.05, cluster size >100 voxels). When combined, OCD patients showed no significant group-level GMV differences versus HCs.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Modest sample size requiring careful robustness checks; need for independent dataset validation; restricted to first-episode treatment-naive patients, limiting generalizability to more heterogeneous samples (e.g., patients with recurrent episodes or comorbidities); alcohol and tobacco use not controlled; obsessive symptom dimensions not recorded, preventing examination of factor-symptom dimension associations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Novel framework combining normative modeling and NMF with automatic K selection via stability maximization across 100 NMF runs with Hungarian matching. Separated positive and negative deviations prior to NMF. Reconciled subject- and group-level findings by regressing group T-map on identified factors, demonstrating that group-level differences represent an 'average patient' not representative of most individuals. Framework generalizes to unseen patients via LOOCV. All participants were Han Chinese and right-handed. Educational level was significantly lower in OCD patients versus HCs (mean 11.776±3.118 vs 13.562±4.492 years, P<0.001). Y-BOCS mean score: 21.929±7.137. Mean illness duration: 4.034±4.810 years. Mean age of onset: 18.341±7.658 years.

general_notes.general_notes: Single-site study at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University using 3T GE Discovery MR750 scanner. All participants were Han Chinese and right-handed. Inclusion criteria: first-episode drug-naive OCD patients diagnosed by two experienced psychiatrists according to DSM-V; no nervous system disease, brain trauma, comorbid psychiatric disorders, first-degree relatives with mental disorder history, or neurological diseases. Exclusion criteria: drugs (anesthetics, analgesics) in past month; substance abuse; brain tumor/trauma/surgery or organic body diseases; cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, or hypertension; MRI contraindications; structural brain abnormalities. CAT12 VBM preprocessing with 1.5 mm isotropic resampling and 6-mm FWHM smoothing; TIV computed. Group-level analyses (SPM12) controlled for age, sex, and TIV. Educational level significantly lower in OCD versus HCs (11.776±3.118 vs 13.562±4.492 years, P<0.001). Image quality (IQR) did not differ between groups (P=0.963). No significant group-level GMV differences between all OCD patients and HCs (two-sample t-test, FDR P<0.05). Published as Open Access by Oxford University Press in Cerebral Cortex (2023). Data available on request.
